_status: MEASURED 2026-09-10/11 on 5e2e0e4, the first controlled re-run under the current harness. All three sequences rate-checked from message stamps (91-94% of realtime), so none is a starved run. robot_localization is the control: its code does not change between FusionCore runs, so a sequence where RL moved is not a valid comparison. On 2013-04-05 RL moved 17%, traced to 93f04d8 (18 Aug) flipping use_odometry_yaw in navsat_transform.yaml four days after the previous baseline was recorded, so that sequence is marked void rather than regressed. Everything measured before 18 Aug 2026 is non-comparable and the old 54.6 / 101.3 entries must not be quoted.

2012-06-15.note: Long-blackout loss, issue #63: one 461.5 s GNSS gap, 13.9% of the run. Local accuracy is NOT the problem: RPE@10m 22.33 m against RL's 22.53 m. Aligning on the pre-blackout segment only, FusionCore tracks to 4.74 m median while fixes are present (RL 3.65 m), reaches 397.7 m at the end of the blackout (RL 72.8 m), and is still 277.2 m out 300 s after 5 Hz fixes return, where RL is back to 17.4 m within 30 s. The failure to re-acquire was a chi2 lockout, fixed in d2a41f2; this entry predates that fix.

2012-08-20.note: Long-blackout loss, issue #64. The outlier cluster at the blackout boundary is a red herring: a physical gate rejects it cleanly and ATE barely moves, because the damage is dead reckoning after the cluster. Config-sensitive through gnss.max_speed, so re-run it after any change to that gate. Predates d2a41f2.

FusionCore still beats RL here (201.10 vs 268.64). Re-record both sides together before using this sequence to judge anything.

_read_this_before_judging_any_regression: This filter is chaotic at the microsecond level while quaternion covariance is unbounded (tools/repro/sensitivity.cpp, and tools/repro/README.md 'What this settles'). Eight runs of 2013-04-05 on identical code and data returned FusionCore 32 m to 345 m, a 9x spread, with achieved-filter-rate correlation r=+0.05 so it is not CPU load. A SINGLE run is therefore not evidence of anything, and regression_threshold_pct of 10 is far inside the noise. Treat a single-run diff as a prompt to re-run, never as a verdict, and prefer a median over at least three runs plus the error distribution (median and fraction over 50 m) to ATE RMSE, which on a heavy-tailed distribution measures the tail rather than the accuracy.
